title: Connection test cannot be cancelled and tests different rows than the one right-clicked
existing_state: TestSelectedConnections (Form1.cs:8875-8961) creates _connectionTestCts (8899) and even handles OperationCanceledException with a "Connection test cancelled" status (8949-8953), but no code path ever calls Cancel() — the only references to _connectionTestCts in the entire file are the declaration (212), creation (8899-8900) and disposal (8958-8959). With the hardcoded SemaphoreSlim(5) concurrency (8910) and timeout of config.ConnectionTimeout seconds per host (8903), right-clicking "Test Connection(s)" with 200 checked rows of unreachable hosts locks the user into a multi-minute unstoppable run (re-entry is blocked by _isTestingConnections at 8877). Separately, the targeting is surprising: the menu item lives on the row context menu, but checked rows always win (8882-8887) and the right-clicked row is only used when nothing is checked (8889-8894) — right-clicking host X while others are checked tests the others, not X.
recommendation: While a test is running, swap the "Test Connection(s)" menu item (or add a status-bar button next to statusProgress) to "Cancel Test" wired to _connectionTestCts.Cancel() — the downstream handling already exists. For targeting, split the menu into two explicit items whose visibility/captions are set in the context-menu Opening handler: "Test This Host" (right-clicked row) and "Test Checked Hosts (N)", mirroring the Run button's existing "Run Checked (N)" convention (UpdateRunButtonText).
user_benefit: A mis-click no longer costs minutes of frozen progress against dead hosts, and the menu does what it says — testing the host you right-clicked instead of silently testing a different set.

evidence.note: CTS created/disposed; grep confirms no .Cancel() caller anywhere
checked rows override the right-clicked row
